Lida Pavlova, the worldwide witch on Instagram: "Ostara is a pagan festival celebrating the Spring Equinox in the Northern Hemisphere.
This year, it falls on March 20, but the spirit and magic of Ostara stay much longer.

Light and darkness, day and night, winter and summer, rest and work—all calls to balance and harmony during the Equinox season. I’m telling here about the goddesses, magic, rituals, meaning and symbolism of Ostara…

And, of course, we’ll see how we can celebrate it today, my dear magical beings!👆🏼👉🏼

Have a blessed Ostara 🪺
With love and a bit of subtle sorcery, 
Lida @lidapavlova_magic"
content.text: Ostara is a pagan festival celebrating the Spring Equinox in the Northern Hemisphere.This year, it falls on March 20, but the spirit and magic of Ostara stay much longer.Light and darkness, day and night, winter and summer, rest and work—all calls to balance and harmony during the Equinox season. I’m telling here about the goddesses, magic, rituals, meaning and symbolism of Ostara…And, of course, we’ll see how we can celebrate it today, my dear magical beings!👆🏼👉🏼Have a blessed Ostara 🪺With love and a bit of subtle sorcery, Lida @lidapavlova_magicDon’t forget Persephone!!🌷Ostara is not a pagan festival. It was created by Gerald Gardner as a Sabbat of Wicca. He got the name from the Germanic goddess Ostara, meaning April lol. The only account of it being a Pagan holiday was from Bebe referencing how they would have feasts for the goddess Estore. Please do your research. I recommend reading Stations of the Sun. ☀️And, as usual, I’ll be sharing posts on Mabon (the autumnal equinox) for the Southern Hemisphere—on March 20, in my stories🤝🏼♥️The pysanka, or egg decorated through a wax resist process, is also a national symbol of Ukraine.
